date_note: Date the CDP's quarterly report no. 03-2026 was circulated to the press, per SocialNetLink (published 21 November); the dates of the plenary decisions are not stated.
exec: A national data protection authority rejected a retailer's facial recognition declaration and referred a data breach complaint to the prosecutor.
org: Commission de Protection des Données Personnelles (CDP)
plain: Senegal's data protection authority did not accept a supermarket's plan to use facial recognition in its video surveillance, and sent a complaint about a personal data breach involving Sen-CSU and Wave to the prosecutor.
summary: According to SocialNetLink's account of the CDP's quarterly report no. 03-2026, the Senegalese data protection authority rejected, "as it stands", a declaration by Sénégal Auchan Store for its Yoff Layène store covering video surveillance with "expert systems such as facial recognition". It also referred a complaint about a "personal data breach" against Sen-CSU and Wave Sénégal to the public prosecutor. SocialNetLink had not obtained reactions from the parties.
title: Senegal's CDP rejects Auchan facial recognition declaration, refers Sen-CSU and Wave complaint to prosecutor

validation.note: SocialNetLink read (relays the CDP's quarterly report); the CDP report itself was not linked or read. No other publisher found.
